assessment.nobel_worthiness: A highly consequential and durable account of how trade exposure, technology, and task change reshape local labour demand and inequality.
assessment.attribution: Autor, Dorn, and Hanson form a coherent core for the empirical and conceptual contribution; the broader literature necessarily has additional important contributors.
assessment.maturity: The evidence has accumulated over many years and has transformed research and policy discussion of labour-market adjustment.
uncertainties: The relative importance of trade, automation, and other concurrent forces remains contested.
Restricting recognition to three names leaves out relevant contributors, including Lawrence F. Katz.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population administrative data have made intergenerational mobility a measurable, geographically precise, and policy-relevant empirical research program.
assessment.attribution: Chetty, Hendren, and Friedman are central to the linked measurement and mobility work represented here.
assessment.maturity: The approach is well established and has generated a substantial body of follow-on research across settings.
uncertainties: Interpretation of geographical mobility correlations as causal policy guidance requires caution.
Lawrence F. Katz is also an important credited contributor.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The modern analysis of monopsony shifted the understanding of wage setting and employer power, with wide implications for minimum wages and labour-market policy.
assessment.attribution: Manning is the clearest single intellectual anchor for the modern monopsony framework, while Ashenfelter and Naidu represent major complementary contributions.
assessment.maturity: The ideas have endured and gained broad empirical relevance as new employer-level evidence has emerged.
uncertainties: The empirical size and institutional sources of employer power vary greatly across labour markets.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This body of work established that early-life health and environments have persistent economic consequences and sharpened the economics of human-capital formation.
assessment.attribution: Currie, Almond, and Cunha represent complementary empirical and theoretical pillars of the contribution.
assessment.maturity: Long-run evidence and extensive subsequent work make the research mature and societally important.
uncertainties: Specific mechanisms and the portability of estimates across institutional settings remain uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Audit and correspondence experiments made discrimination directly measurable in realistic labour-market interactions and altered empirical practice.
assessment.attribution: Bertrand and Mullainathan are central to the influential experimental demonstration; Charles is also a major scholar of racial inequality.
assessment.maturity: The design has been replicated widely and remains foundational to research on discrimination.
uncertainties: Correspondence-study results identify important stages of hiring but do not by themselves describe all mechanisms of labour-market inequality.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The integration of taxable-income evidence with optimal-tax theory has made behavioural responses central to practical public-finance analysis.
assessment.attribution: Saez, Chetty, and Slemrod provide a strong bridge between theory, empirical elasticities, and tax-policy application; Stantcheva is also a substantial contributor.
assessment.maturity: The framework has had lasting influence on academic research and tax-policy debate.
uncertainties: Estimated taxable-income elasticities depend on institutions, enforcement, and margins of adjustment.
Normative conclusions depend on social-welfare assumptions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Structural analysis of labour supply and household intertemporal choices has provided core tools for evaluating taxes and transfer policy.
assessment.attribution: Blundell, Meghir, and MaCurdy are leading contributors to the structural empirical tradition represented by the candidate.
assessment.maturity: The methods are long established and retain substantial influence in public and labour economics.
uncertainties: Structural conclusions can be sensitive to modelling assumptions and the policy environment used for estimation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Research on teacher quality, school performance, and educational production has significantly improved the empirical basis for education policy.
assessment.attribution: Kane, Hanushek, and Woessmann represent influential strands of the evidence; Hoxby is likewise an important credited contributor.
assessment.maturity: The field has accumulated extensive evidence and has direct relevance for policy design.
uncertainties: Measures of teacher and school effectiveness can be sensitive to design choices and are difficult to translate into scalable policy.
The contribution is broad and attribution among several leading researchers is not uniquely determined.
